Subject: Vendor onboarding / VAT split and PO attestation questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're starting Alder Systems' vendor onboarding for Redwood and have a couple of items to confirm before we create the PO in our system:

- We need a formal attestation from Redwood confirming which legal entity will receive payment and that Redwood will accept a split PO (Alder has separate remit entities for product and services, and we require an attestation so our AP system can allocate VAT correctly).
- For EU invoices where reverse-charge applies, does Redwood provide VAT identifiers on the invoice line level, or will you accept a single consolidated VAT field + attestation?
- Any sample AP packet or required fields you can send so we can pre-populate our vendor record and avoid re-submissions?

We can expedite internally if we have a short checklist and a signed attestation PDF. Please CC our procurement alias (procurement@alder.com) and finance (finance@alder.com) on the response.

Appreciate it — Olivia

Olivia Grant

Subject: RE: Vendor onboarding / VAT split and PO attestation questions

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the note. I've pulled together a short preflight checklist and the documents we typically provide when being registered as a vendor in a customer's AP system. Attached: Alder_AP_Onboarding_Packet.pdf (fillable), vendor-self-attestation.xlsx, and our standard vendor terms. Highlights below so your team can map fields into your vendor portal quickly:

1) Remit/legal entity: Please confirm the remit entity name exactly as it should appear on the PO ("Redwood Inference, Inc." vs "Redwood EMEA Ltd."). If the PO will be split across legal entities, we require an attestation form for each Redwood entity receiving funds.

2) PO attestation: We can provide a signed vendor attestation (PDF) that states the payment split and which entity will invoice for which line items. For automated processing, we recommend Alder attach that attestation to the PO record.

3) VAT handling: For EU reverse-charge scenarios we include our VAT number at the invoice header and add a note on the affected line items. If Alder requires VAT per-line identifiers, we can provide them but that usually requires a minor invoice template change.

4) Required fields for your portal: vendor legal name, VAT ID, remit address, bank details (IBAN), contact email, PO acceptance policy (Net terms), and attestation reference.

Next steps:
- If you confirm the remit entities and whether the PO will be split now, Marcus (cc'd) can prepare the attestation and sign it digitally.
- If you prefer DocuSign, we can send the attestation via a DocuSign envelope (I'll include a link).

I've attached the packet and a blank attestation sheet. Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call if you want to walk through the mapping.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Thanks Rachel — that's helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Our preferred flow is to create a single PO with split line-level accounting across two Alder remit entities. We require a signed vendor attestation confirming Redwood will invoice the appropriate lines under the correct legal entity.
- For reverse-charge, our AP system currently expects a VAT indicator on each invoice line. If Redwood can include a line-level flag (RCY) plus your VAT registration number on the header, that will satisfy our automation.

If you can prepare the attestation with an explicit mapping of "Line 1 -> Redwood EMEA Ltd (VAT 12345678)" and "Line 2 -> Redwood Inference, Inc. (VAT N/A)", we can run the vendor through our portal without manual review.

Also looping in our procurement lead (procurement@alder.com) to expedite the PO creation. Can you confirm estimated turnaround if Marcus signs and we accept the sample packet?

Best,
Olivia
